content: Avenanthramides are a class of phytoalexins found predominantly in the groats of oat seeds. These compounds are part of a group of at least 25 avenanthramides, which differ based on the substituents present on their cinnamic acid and anthranilic acid rings. Among these, three specific avenanthramides are most abundant in oat grains: avenanthramide C (Bc), avenanthramide B (Bf), and avenanthramide A (Bp). In vitro studies have demonstrated that these compounds exhibit significant antioxidant activity, with the potency ranking as Bc > Bf > Bp. This antioxidant capacity has been shown to confer various health benefits in both human and animal studies. These benefits include a reduction in the rate of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) oxidation, as well as protective effects against cancers and cardiovascular diseases.
